summary: The second-to-second layer is genuinely deep — a graded hit-stop/bloom/shake ladder per outcome, a 3-beat shot (reticle snap → tracer → settle), per-tile footfalls, pose deformation (recoil/flinch/lean), enemy intent telegraphs, and a 13-cue procedural sound set — and DESIGN §4 grades it "Strong". Reading the code against that grade, the gaps are concentrated in four places: (1) motion — every multi-tile walk eases in-and-out at every tile so units caterpillar instead of glide, and VAULT slides straight through the cover it claims to leap; (2) beats that are claimed but not built — the "slow-mo kill-cam" is a hard 0.4 s freeze during which its own zoom-punch decays to nothing, and `ShotAnim.Reaction` is never read by any presentation code so an overwatch trigger plays as an ordinary shot with the same cue as setting overwatch; (3) audio coverage — no explosion cue exists (grenade/barrel/siege play "crit"+"death"; heal/hack/beacon/stabilize play "reload"; smoke/shove play "hunker"); (4) readability collisions — same-frame floating texts overprint (BRACE damage + STAGGERED 4 px apart; a KIA fires three strings inside 24 px), and the first enemy's intent telegraph each turn runs under the ENEMY TURN banner's centre band. Every item below is verifiable headlessly with an existing hook (LONGMOVE per-frame Pos dump, SHOTSEQ filmstrip, AUDIOTEST/AUDIOGATE, FITTEST) or a small new PASS/FAIL leg routed through qa-sweep's verdict; nothing needs a display beyond the screenshot harness.

findings.title: Multi-tile movement eases in-and-out at EVERY tile — units caterpillar instead of glide
findings.evidence: src/Anim.cs:40 `_dur = diag ? 0.155f : 0.12f` (one tile per anim) and src/Anim.cs:61 `Unit.Pos = Vector2.Lerp(_from, _to, Util.EaseInOutQuad(k))`. Paths are enqueued as N independent MoveStepAnims at src/Game.cs:5561 (IssueMove), :7345/:7403 (enemy moves), :4461 (pod scatter), :6671 (VIP leash), src/Game.Harness.cs:8859. WalkLean is re-kicked to 1 at every OnStart (Anim.cs:43) and decays at 7.5/s (Game.cs:3890). DEVLOG §W5-B's LONGMOVE filmstrip only counted 'backwards steps', never velocity continuity.
findings.problem: EaseInOutQuad velocity is 0 at both ends and 2x the mean at mid-tile; at 0.12 s/tile (~7 frames at 60 fps) a six-tile walk is six accelerate/brake cycles with a lean re-kick each time. The most frequent action in the game reads as a pulsing stutter rather than a stride, on both teams (the enemy turn is mostly movement). Pillar 2 'feels good' — tweened motion is named as its first example.
findings.proposal: Give MoveStepAnim a segment flag (First / Mid / Last / Single) set by the six enqueue sites (a tiny helper `EnqueuePath(unit, path, team)` in Game.cs replaces the foreach loops). Update(): Single → EaseInOutQuad (today), First → EaseInQuad, Mid → linear, Last → EaseOutQuad; set WalkLean only on First. Leave `_dur` and the `k >= 1` commit + `OnUnitEnteredTile` call untouched so overwatch timing, the STACKTEST probe and PAIRTEST are unaffected (Unit.Pos is presentation).
findings.acceptance: `SIGHTLINE_LONGMOVE=1 SIGHTLINE_SHOT=<n>` already dumps the unit's tweened Pos every frame (Program.cs:1138-1139, Game.Harness.cs:8839): compute per-frame speed and assert min mid-path speed ≥ 60% of max and zero frames under 40% of mean (today it hits ~0 at every tile boundary). Add that as a PASS/FAIL line routed through qa-sweep's `verdict`. `SIGHTLINE_PAIRTEST=1` byte-identical; `SIGHTLINE_SHOTSEQ=48 SIGHTLINE_AUTOPLAY=1` filmstrip for eyes.

findings.title: The 'slow-mo kill-cam' is a hard 0.4 s freeze — and its own zoom-punch decays to ~1% while frozen
findings.evidence: src/Game.cs:3957 `if (HitStop > 0) { HitStop -= dt * AnimSpeed; return; }` returns BEFORE `Fx.Update(t)` (~3973) and the anim pump (~4010). KillUnit's mission-ending arm src/Game.cs:3227-3233 adds `AddHitStop(0.4f)` + `AddZoomPunch(0.13f)`, but `_camPulse *= MathF.Exp(-dt * 11f)` at src/Game.cs:3938 runs above the return, so after 0.4 s the pulse is exp(-4.4) ≈ 1.2%. The shatter FX spawned at 3197-3200 sit at frame 0 for 0.4 s then play at full speed. docs/FEATURES.md:416 and docs/ROADMAP.md 3.11 both describe this as 'lingers in slow-mo'.
findings.problem: The single most important beat in a mission (last hostile / squad wipe / VIP lost) is a still image: tracer, shockwave, sparks and camera all stop dead, then everything snaps to full speed. The zoom that was meant to punch the moment spends itself invisibly inside the freeze. Doc over-claim of the exact kind CLAUDE.md warns about (juice graded on something nobody watched).
findings.proposal: Add `Game.TimeScale` (default 1). Keep `HitStop` binary for the ≤0.1 s hit/crit/kill freezes. For `IsMissionEndingKill` set `_killCam = 0.45f` and while it runs: skip the early return, multiply `t` by 0.25 for `Fx.Update`, the anim pump dt, and `DecayUnitFx`; hold `_camPulse` (no decay) until `_killCam` expires, then let it relax. Under `AutoPlay` keep TimeScale 1 so frame counts don't move. Fix the two doc lines to say what ships.
findings.acceptance: New headless leg (e.g. in DEATHTEST or a `SIGHTLINE_FEELTEST`): stage a last-hostile kill, step `Update(1/60)` for 30 frames and assert (a) a tracked particle's Pos changes every frame (today: zero delta for 24 frames), (b) mean per-frame displacement ≈ 0.25x the post-window rate, (c) `_camPulse` ≥ 50% of its peak at frame 24. Route through verdict. Autoplay x3 frame counts unchanged. `SIGHTLINE_SHOTSEQ` filmstrip of the final blow for eyes.

findings.title: Overwatch REACTION shots have no distinct beat — same cue as SETTING overwatch, same wind-up as a normal shot, `ShotAnim.Reaction` unread by presentation
findings.evidence: src/Game.cs:3044-3050 (OnUnitEnteredTile): `PopText("OVERWATCH")` 18px + `Audio.Play("over")` then `_anims.Insert(.., new ShotAnim(w, mover, res, reaction: true))`. The identical `"over"` cue is played by DoOverwatch (Game.cs:5642), FOCUS/BRACE (5689/5710/5747), CONTACT! (4472), a 'charge whine stand-in' (7033) and two more enemy verbs (7133/7154). src/Anim.cs:174 `public bool Reaction` — the only consumer in the repo is Game.cs:3138 (RECLAIMER boon); Renderer.cs/Hud.cs contain zero references. ShotAnim wind-up is the flat `WindUp = 0.10f` (Anim.cs:~181) regardless.
findings.problem: The genre's signature 'gotcha' — a body steps into a held lane — is indistinguishable from an ordinary shot at a moving target, and 'I armed overwatch' and 'my overwatch just fired' are the same sound. DESIGN §3.B asks that failure be legible and telegraphed; the player's OWN soldier walking into an enemy lane gets the same non-event, which is exactly the moment stakes should bite.
findings.proposal: In `ShotAnim.OnStart` when `Reaction` (and not `_windless`): WindUp 0.10 → 0.26 s, `g.AddHitStop(0.06f)`, a larger team-tinted `ReticleSnap` (r0 40 → r1 16) plus an `Fx.Flash` on the MOVER, and set the mover's `FlinchAnim` to 0.4 (a caught-in-the-open freeze). Register a `react` cue in `Audio.BuildRecipes` (a sharp descending two-note snap next to `"over"` at Audio.cs:282) and play it at Game.cs:3045 instead of `"over"`. Keep `_windless` collapsing all of it under AutoPlay so balance/smoke frame counts are unchanged.
findings.acceptance: Headless leg (STAGGERTEST/OWTEST style): construct a reaction ShotAnim with `g.AutoPlay=false`, call OnStart, assert `FireAt` ≈ 0.30 vs 0.14 for a normal shot and that `g.HitStop > 0` immediately after OnStart. `SIGHTLINE_AUDIOTEST=1` / `SIGHTLINE_AUDIOGATE=1` PASS with `react` added to gameIds (Audio.cs:955), SfxCueIds (Audio.cs:994) and CatOf (Audio.Analysis.cs:420-428). Autoplay x3 frame= values identical to pre-change.

findings.title: No explosion cue exists — grenade/barrel/siege play 'crit'+'death'; heal/hack/beacon/stabilize play 'reload'; smoke/shove play 'hunker'
findings.evidence: The whole gameplay cue set is 13 ids (src/Audio.cs:193-304 BuildRecipes; gameIds Audio.cs:955-956; SfxCueIds Audio.cs:994-1000) and none is a detonation. GrenadeAnim.Explode src/Anim.cs:529-530 `Audio.Play("crit")`+`Audio.Play("death")`; DetonateBarrel src/Game.cs:3739 and DetonateSiege :3694 the same pair; FlashAnim Anim.cs:767 and IncendiaryAnim :799 `"crit"`; SmokeAnim :747 and ShoveAnim :111 `"hunker"`; HealAnim :861, DoStabilize Game.cs:3431, DoHack :5781/:5792, DoBeacon :5842/:5874 and the ability sites :6129-6219 all `"reload"`; IssueDrag :5479 `"move"`. A2 (DEVLOG §A2) gave the five weapons voices but left every non-weapon verb on a borrowed UI cue.
findings.problem: The largest single event in the game (frag/barrel: shake 12-14, the biggest bloom spike, a 0.07 hit-stop) is voiced as 'a crit landed and a soldier collapsed'; a corpsman's heal sounds like a magazine change; a flashbang and an incendiary are both 'crit'. Audio is the channel that lets a player follow the enemy turn without watching every tile, and right now five different verbs share one sound.
findings.proposal: Register four procedural cues in `BuildRecipes`: `boom` (sub sine 48→28 Hz + a 1.2 kHz→180 Hz noise wash, ~0.6 s, ~-4 dBFS peak, no detune), `flash` (3 kHz ping + short white burst, 0.2 s), `heal` (rising sine triad, 0.3 s, 'ui' category), `smoke` (soft band-limited hiss, 0.4 s). Route the sites above (grenade/barrel/siege → boom; flashbang → flash; incendiary → boom at -6 dB; smoke → smoke; heal/stabilize → heal). Add the ids to gameIds, SfxCueIds, CatOf (Audio.Analysis.cs:420-428), and a `boom+death+st_kill` row to `Stacks` (Audio.Analysis.cs:245-253) so the limiter budget covers the new worst case. The file-first loader then also honours `assets/sfx/boom.ogg` if the owner ever drops one in.
findings.acceptance: `SIGHTLINE_AUDIOTEST=1` and `SIGHTLINE_AUDIOGATE=1` print PASS with the new ids (the gate's stack headroom check must still clear -1 dBFS with the boom row). `SIGHTLINE_AUDIODUMP=1` writes boom/flash/heal/smoke .wav for the human to audition; add their one-line descriptions at Audio.cs:1385-1396 so AUDIO CHECK lists them. `grep -n 'Audio.Play("crit")' src/Anim.cs src/Game.cs` shows no detonation site left.

findings.title: Floating combat text overprints itself: same-frame pops at one anchor rise in lockstep for their whole 1.1 s life
findings.evidence: src/Fx.cs PopText (~380-410): `Rise` is a constant 46 px/s, `Drift` is 0 for any size ≤ 26 (`weight = (size-26)/10`), and for larger sizes the direction is a hash of (text, x, y) — identical strings at one anchor get identical trajectories. Concrete same-frame collisions: BRACE hit → damage number at D.Pos-26 (src/Anim.cs:337) and 'STAGGERED' at D.Pos-30 (Anim.cs:365), 4 px apart; any kill → the number at -26 (337) + KillUnit's 'KIA'/'DOWN' at -10 (src/Game.cs:3204, 22 px) + the 30 px `KIA  NAME` stamp at -34 (Game.cs:3216) — three strings inside 24 px; two overwatch hits for equal damage → two identical '3's with the same hash → same drift; grenade → per-unit number at -26 plus the KIA trio on a kill.
findings.problem: The exact moments the text is supposed to explain (a stagger, a kill, a multi-reaction) are the ones where it becomes an unreadable glyph pile. DESIGN §3.C: 'juice must serve clarity, not bury it'.
findings.proposal: In `Fx.PopText` and `Fx.Stamp`, before adding: count live `Texts` whose Pos is within 22 px of `at` (n) and offset the new one by n×16 px upward, alternating ±18 px laterally for odd n; salt the drift hash with a per-call counter so two identical numbers diverge. Optionally colour the damage number by VICTIM team (today `numCol` at Anim.cs:~335 is the same off-white whether it is your soldier or theirs) — one job per accent, DESIGN §3.H.
findings.acceptance: New headless leg (`SIGHTLINE_FEELTEST` or an FX leg in an existing test): spawn PopText('3') twice at one point plus Stamp at -34, step one frame, assert every pairwise distance ≥ 14 px (today: 0 px for the twin '3's, 4 px for STAGGERED). Route through verdict. `SIGHTLINE_KIA=1` screenshot and a BRACE-hit `SIGHTLINE_SHOTSEQ` frame for eyes.

findings.title: VAULT animates as a straight 0.12 s slide THROUGH the cover it is supposed to leap
findings.evidence: src/Game.cs:5538 `Enqueue(new MoveStepAnim(u, tx, ty), Team.Player)` — a single step for a 2-tile straight hop over a cover tile. MoveStepAnim derives `_dur` from `diag` only (src/Anim.cs:40: 0.12 s for a straight 2-tile hop, i.e. 2x walking speed) and lerps a straight line with no Y component (Anim.cs:61), so the figure's centre passes through the cover volume's rect. GrenadeAnim already has the arc math (`ArcAt`, Anim.cs:~625). No DEVLOG mention of a vault arc.
findings.problem: A verb named VAULT, popped as 'VAULT' (Game.cs:5536), reads as a teleport-slide through a wall. It also spends only one footfall cue for a 2-tile move. Pillar 2 and pillar 4: the motion contradicts the rule the player was just told.
findings.proposal: Add `public float Hop` (arc height px, default 0) and an optional `DurOverride` to MoveStepAnim; IssueVault sets Hop=26, dur 0.24 s. In Update add `-MathF.Sin(k*PI)*Hop` to `Unit.Pos.Y`, raise `WalkLean` to 1.4 for the crouch, and call `g.Fx.Dust` at landing (k≥1). Leave the commit/`OnUnitEnteredTile` path untouched.
findings.acceptance: A `SIGHTLINE_VAULTTEST` leg (or a FIELDTEST extension): stage a vault, step the anim at 1/60, assert peak Y lift ≥ 20 px mid-flight and final `Unit.Pos == TileCenter(tx,ty)`; PAIRTEST byte-identical; `SIGHTLINE_SHOTSEQ` filmstrip of a vault for eyes.

findings.title: The first enemy's INTENT telegraph every turn plays underneath the ENEMY TURN banner's centre band
findings.evidence: src/Game.cs:6426-6427 (EndPlayerTurn): `ShowBanner("ENEMY TURN", true)` — BannerMax 1.2 s at Game.cs:2849 — then `Enqueue(new WaitAnim(0.5f))`. UpdateEnemy's PickNext then holds `TelegraphBeat = 0.5f` (Game.cs:234, enqueued at 6962) with `IntentUnit` set, so the telegraph runs t≈0.5-1.0 s. `BannerTimer` decrements every frame independent of the anim queue (Game.cs:~3990, above the pump). Hud.DrawBanner (src/Hud.cs:2465-2490) paints a full-width 92 px band at `ScreenH/2-46` at alpha 0.72 in the HUD layer (over the board), full until t=0.7 and fading to 1.2. DEVLOG §FUL-4 review noted the same collision as a harness nuisance ('the banner lives ~72 frames, so SHOT=90 photographs an empty telegraph') without seeing the player-facing overlap.
findings.problem: The 'it's about to hit you' warning (Renderer.cs:1940-1947: 'deliberately bold') for the first hostile each turn is drawn with its path/target's middle rows behind a dark scrim. The one telegraph the player is guaranteed to need — the opener of every enemy turn — is the one they can least see.
findings.proposal: Cheapest: make the opening WaitAnim equal to the banner's visible life (`BannerMax`, or shorten both ENEMY/PLAYER TURN banners to 0.8 s and wait 0.8). Alternative that preserves pacing: in PickNext, if `BannerTimer > 0.3f` enqueue a `WaitAnim(BannerTimer - 0.3f)` before the telegraph beat. Either is a two-line change in Game.cs.
findings.acceptance: Headless assertion (STALLTEST-style leg): with `AutoPlay=false, NoPersist=true`, call EndPlayerTurn and step Update(1/60) until `IntentUnit != null`; assert `BannerTimer <= 0.3f` (today it reads ~0.7). `SIGHTLINE_INTENT=1` screenshot at the telegraph frame shows no band over the drawn path.

findings.title: Grenade/item targeting previews the footprint but not the consequence — no per-unit damage/kill forecast, no friendly-fire warning, no cover-crack preview
findings.evidence: src/Renderer.cs:4101-4137 DrawGrenade: range ring + 3x3 tile tint + arc + two circles; DrawItem :4158-4185 the same. The resolution in GrenadeAnim.Explode (src/Anim.cs:~545-600) deals 3-5 to BOTH teams, ignores cover, cracks cover via `Grid.DamageCover`, wakes pods and sets Burning — none of it shown before the click. Hud.cs references GrenadeMode only at :1427 (button) and :2383 (threat-card suppression); there is no grenade card, while the SHOT path gets the full odds tooltip (Hud.DrawTooltip 2091-2311). ROADMAP.md:33 records 'hits BOTH teams (friendly fire)' as a rule.
findings.problem: The shot verb honours the perfect-information contract; the blast verbs do not. A player learns friendly fire and pod-waking by doing them — output feedback for what should be input information (DESIGN §3.B, §3.E 'make affordances obvious').
findings.proposal: In DrawGrenade (and DrawItem for flash/incendiary): for each alive unit in the footprint draw a team-tinted ring and a small label — '3-5' (through `Combat.HardenedReduce` and the fragile floor) or 'KILL' when `Hp <= minDmg`; if any soldier/VIP is inside, tint the footprint Pal.Foe and caption the reticle 'FRIENDLY FIRE'; dash-outline cover tiles that will crack; add a '+WAKES POD' caption when a dormant enemy is in the radius. All draw-only, reading the same constants Explode uses.
findings.acceptance: `SIGHTLINE_GRENSHOT=1` screenshot hook staging a footprint containing one soldier, one enemy and one low-cover tile; a FITTEST-style `Cfg.InkProbe` assertion that the 'FRIENDLY FIRE' string is present when a soldier is in the footprint and absent otherwise, and that every label lands inside the board rect. CB pass with `SIGHTLINE_CB=1`.

findings.title: A bare left-click on any targetable enemy FIRES immediately (no arm step), unlike every other targeted verb
findings.evidence: src/Game.cs:4975-4977 (BoardAct, outside AimMode): `hovered.Team == Team.Enemy && Selected.CanAct && CanTarget(...) → IssueShoot(hovered)`. IssueShoot (Game.cs:5568-5606) spends ammo, an action, sets FiredThisTurn and calls BreakConcealment at :5573. Grenade/item/shove/drag/vault/mark/grapple/pin all require a Toggle → click pair (BoardAct :4919-4973). The hover tooltip shows odds first (Hud.DrawTooltip), which mitigates. grep of DEVLOG/DESIGN for click-to-fire/misclick rationale: none.
findings.problem: The one irreversible, concealment-breaking verb is the only one with zero friction; a click intended to inspect a foe (or that lands on a foe standing on the tile you meant to walk to) opens the fight. XCOM-style convention is select-target → confirm. This trades a real misclick cost for snappiness the arm step barely dents.
findings.proposal: Route the :4975 branch to `EnterAim(false); AimTarget = hovered;` so the first click locks the target (DrawAim's spinning reticle + odds confirm it) and the second fires; keep key `1` and the keyboard Space path as they are. Optionally a Display 'ONE-CLICK FIRE' toggle on the pause card for veterans. This is a judgement call — record it as an owner decision if not shipped.
findings.acceptance: TRUTHTEST/SNAPTEST-style headless leg: with AimMode=false, simulate BoardAct on an enemy tile, assert Ammo and ActionsLeft unchanged, `AimMode == true`, `AimTarget == enemy`; a second BoardAct fires (ammo-1). Autoplay unaffected (SmartStep/AutoStep never route through BoardAct); autoplay x3 identical.

findings.title: A MISS gives the target no reaction and does not tell the player the odds it beat
findings.evidence: src/Anim.cs:371-383: on a miss the tracer endpoint scatters ±22 px, 5 grey sparks + 4 ricochet sparks fire, and 'MISS' pops at 24 px in Pal.TxtDim; `D.Flash`, `D.FlinchAnim`, `D.Recoil` are untouched (the hit branch sets all three at :255-262 / :293-296). The rolled % goes only to the combat log (`Stats.Log` at :401), whose panel is off-board and hidden until the first entry (Hud.cs:1181-1188). DESIGN §3.B: 'Don't let a single 85% roll silently decide … with no feedback explaining the odds'.
findings.problem: A round passes a figure's ear and the figure stands like a statue; the player who missed a 90% has to look away from the board to learn it was a 90%. The output-randomness rage surface is exactly where a cheap, honest beat pays most.
findings.proposal: On a miss: set `D.FlinchAnim = 0.35f` with the lateral-only shudder (the pose already exists in DrawUnit, Renderer.cs:~3425), a 1.5 px `D.Recoil` away from the tracer, and pop `MISS 87%` (append `Res.Odds.HitChance`, % in Pal.Accent when ≥ 70 so a 'robbed' roll reads as such); a short `Fx.ImpactStreak` at the scattered endpoint. Keep the enemy-miss pop plain 'MISS' if the % is judged too noisy on the enemy turn.
findings.acceptance: TRUTHTEST leg: resolve a forced miss, assert the newest FloatText contains `Res.Odds.HitChance` and `D.FlinchAnim > 0` one frame later. `SIGHTLINE_UNITFX=1` screenshot for the duck pose.

findings.title: On-board OVERWATCH badge is 10 px text ('OW'/'BRC') under the 12 px floor; HUNKER is an unlabelled 6 px diamond
findings.evidence: src/Renderer.cs:3984-3993: `Cfg.Text(u.OwBrace ? "BRC" : "OW", …, 10, …)` inside a 6 px disc; `Raylib.DrawPoly(new Vector2(p.X, p.Y - 35), 4, 6f, 45f, Pal.Good)` for hunker. CLAUDE.md: '12px is the small-text floor'; the C5 survey (ROADMAP 'Left open by C5') measured chrome at 10-11 px but board glyphs were not in it. The action bar already has shape-redundant icons for both verbs (Hud.DrawActionIcon, Hud.cs:1671+: two concentric arcs / chevron-in-shield).
findings.problem: The two most common held stances read as a 10 px abbreviation and a green dot — the focused cone (DrawFocusCones) and enemy lanes (DrawOverwatchThreat) are drawn, but a plain wide watch on your own soldier, the thing you set most turns, is the least legible state on the token. Hue-only for hunker fails the CB rule in DESIGN §3.H.
findings.proposal: Factor DrawActionIcon into a shared `Glyphs.Draw(id, cx, cy, c, scale)` helper (Util.cs or a new Glyphs.cs) and stamp the 14 px overwatch/hunker glyphs above the token, tinted Pal.Accent / Pal.Good, with a slow pulsing ring while a watch is armed; BRACE = the same glyph in Pal.Good plus a short bar under it. Keep 'BRC' text only in the tooltip.
findings.acceptance: `SIGHTLINE_FITTEST=1 SIGHTLINE_FITDUMP=small` lists no 10 px board string; `SIGHTLINE_FOCUSOW=1` and a plain-overwatch/hunker screenshot; `SIGHTLINE_CB=1` pass shows the two states differ by shape, not only hue.

findings.title: No headless probe exists for motion continuity or beat timing — every feel fix is verified by eye
findings.evidence: The closest instruments are the LONGMOVE per-frame Pos dump (src/Program.cs:1138-1139, src/Game.Harness.cs:8839-8861; DEVLOG §W5-B counted only 'backwards steps') and the SHOTSEQ PNG filmstrip (Program.cs:1315-1323). `Fx.AmbientSelfTest` (Fx.cs:~830) proves the pattern of a window-free FX self-test already works. No test reads ShotAnim.FireAt/Total, MoveStepAnim velocity, FloatText separation, or particle displacement during HitStop.
findings.problem: Pillar 2 is the only pillar with no PASS/FAIL line in qa-sweep; the W9 rule ('every fix ships a test proven to FAIL pre-fix') cannot be applied to findings 1-7 without one. CLAUDE.md warns that self-test lines not routed through `verdict` are invisible to the gate.
findings.proposal: Add `SIGHTLINE_FEELTEST=1` in Game.Harness.cs: (a) stage a 6-tile walk and report min/mean/max per-frame speed + frames under 40% of mean; (b) a normal vs reaction ShotAnim, reporting FireAt/Total; (c) a vault, reporting peak Y lift; (d) two PopTexts + a Stamp at one anchor, reporting min pairwise separation after one frame; (e) a mission-ending kill window, reporting per-frame particle displacement and `_camPulse` at frame 24. One `FEELTEST: PASS/FAIL` line, thresholds as constants beside the anims, wired into scripts/qa-sweep.sh via `verdict` and covered by its COVERAGE GUARD.
findings.acceptance: On today's tree the hook prints FAIL for legs (a), (c), (d), (e) and PASS after the fixes above — the proven-to-fail-pre-fix contract. `bash scripts/qa-sweep.sh --full` footer shows the new hook counted and SWEEP-EXIT=0 only when it passes.

summary: The minute-to-minute and run-to-run loops are unusually complete on paper (branching map with kind/faction/objective/class, 17 field events, 16 boons, 5 contracts, a priced veteran reserve, 6 meta unlocks, a 9-rung heat ladder) and unusually well instrumented, but several of the fork's decisions are not decisions when read against DESIGN.md §3.A. The SUPPLY node strictly dominates the modal COMBAT node on every visible axis (fewer bodies, lower stats, more intel, a full heal that also silently cancels the wound gauge) and the ELITE premium is +4 intel over SUPPLY for +3 bodies; the PITCHED/TASKED class is now legible but still unpriced (C3's declared open half); an EVENT node's hover tooltip names an objective it does not have and calls a non-fight "Standard force +0 intel"; and the biome that C4 made mechanical is knowable at the barracks for every column yet appears on no pre-deployment surface. On the run-to-run side, each field event is a ~1-in-9-run sight with the DEVLOG's own recommended fix (profile-side dedupe) unbuilt, the five run contracts have never been priced although the harness plumbing to do so exists, and the WAR ROOM's 330 salvage of unlocks is exhausted after roughly five wins while the heat cap climbs one rung per win at cap. Two small mechanism defects also surfaced: a mid-run AddHeat event silently switches the adaptive assist off for the rest of the run, and heat's intel kicker is paid in full on missions 1-2 where its numeric teeth are graced to zero.

findings.title: SUPPLY strictly dominates COMBAT on the campaign fork, and its full heal silently cancels the wound gauge
findings.evidence: src/Run.cs:905-916 CardForNode: Supply = EnemyDelta -1 / StatDelta -1 / Reward Heal; Combat = 0/0/none; Elite = +2/+1/BonusPerk. src/Run.cs:952-962 NodeIntel: Supply = base+10, Elite = base+14, Combat = base — so Supply out-pays Combat and Elite pays only +4 over Supply for +3 bodies and +2 stat. src/Game.cs:2565 applies the Heal reward (u.Hp = MaxHp) BEFORE src/Game.cs:2572 DebriefSurvivors, and src/Run.cs:1486 gauges the fresh wound from u.Hp (`sev = u.Hp <= MaxHp/4 ? 2 : ...`), so no soldier who finished a Supply clear on their feet can ever be wounded by it — a second, undocumented subsidy. Generator: src/Run.cs:744-745 stamps supplies = max(1, mids/4) (2-3 per map among 8-12 mids), so a Supply is a sibling choice in most columns. Measured: DEVLOG §W1 byNodeKind Supply 94.4% vs Combat 89.2%; DEVLOG §C3 (line ~8211) Decapitate on Supply 67.3% vs Combat 32.9% ("one body and one stat point ... 34 points apart"); DEVLOG §C4 addendum (line ~11474) Supply 89.2 / Combat 78.2 / Elite 72.3 at n≈240-490/arm. findings.problem: Whenever a SUPPLY and a COMBAT node are both reachable, the player-facing information (Light resistance, +more intel, Full squad heal) says take Supply, and the hidden wound-gauge cancellation makes it even better than it reads. The fork's headline trade-off collapses to objective/faction only; ELITE's risk premium is a random-recipient perk plus 4 intel. The batch never samples the human-optimal route, so no ladder number reflects it.
findings.proposal: Price safety. In Run.NodeIntel make Supply pay LESS than Combat (e.g. Supply = base − 4: the heal IS the reward; Combat = base + 6: a faction fight pays; Elite unchanged at base + 14), and either move the Supply/RECON Heal reward in Game.EnterBarracks to AFTER DebriefSurvivors (so the wound gauge still bites and the heal restores HP) or state the wound immunity on the node hover. Update the hover line at Hud.cs:5197 and the deploy card at Hud.cs:5655 so the payout ordering is visible. Ship with SIGHTLINE_ROUTE=hash for the measurement round so Supply is actually sampled (~17% of picks).
findings.acceptance: (1) A ROUTETEST leg asserting NodeIntel ordering Elite > Combat > Supply at equal depth for every seed, and a Run-level leg (TRAITTEST style): a soldier at Hp=1 who clears a Supply node ends the debrief with Wound > 0. findings.title: The campaign-map hover for an EVENT node reads 'EVENT - ELIMINATE / Standard force +0 intel'

findings.title: Field events are a ~1-in-9-run sight each; the DEVLOG's recommended cross-run dedupe is unbuilt
findings.evidence: src/Events.cs:95 EventCatalog.All has 17 entries; src/Run.cs:755 stamps events = Clamp(mids/4, 1, 2) per map; src/Events.cs:295 IndexForNode dedupes only within a run (pure function of MapSeed + map). DEVLOG §FUL-13 '"?"-NODE EXPOSURE LEVER': 'informant and reservecall fielded ZERO times in 200 campaigns ... each event is a ~1-in-9-run sight ... The honest exposure levers are floor-2 stamping (reshapes in-flight saves) or a cross-run catalog dedupe (profile-side, no skew)'. docs/ROADMAP.md OPEN 'Event exposure' carries the same two options. Meta persistence is whole-DTO append-only (src/Meta.cs header, SaveGame).
findings.problem: Run-to-run variety (DESIGN §3.F) is supposed to come from combinations, and the event deck is the loop's only narrative beat; at 1-2 draws per run from 17 a returning player sees the same handful (ABANDONED CACHE, WOUNDED MEDIC) and never meets the FUL-10 forks. In Run.Start (interactive path only; NoPersist → salt 0 = today's selection, byte-identical) try salts 0..N and keep the first whose IndexForNode assignment for this map contains no seen id (fallback: fewest). Mix the salt into Events.Hash so IndexForNode stays a pure function of persisted run state (reload-stable). Append resolved ids to SeenEvents in ResolveEvent under !NoPersist.

PAIRTEST byte-identical. A headless METATEST-style simulation of 20 consecutive runs from one profile prints distinct-events ≥ min(17, draws) versus ~10 expected without dedupe.

The preview under-states the cost precisely for the least-resilient player.

Decide separately whether UnlockHeatOnWin should compare the STARTING heat (record `StartHeat` on the run) — DESIGN says winning AT the cap unlocks; an event-raised finish is arguably earned.

findings.title: Heat's intel kicker is paid in full on missions 1-2 where heat's numeric teeth are graced to zero — the apex's economy is front-loaded and undocumented
findings.evidence: src/Game.cs:2090-2091 (campaign): `if (n <= 1) { heatEnemy = 0; heatStat = 0; heatDmg = 0; } else if (n == 2) { ... /= 2 }`. src/Game.cs:2632 `heatBonus = Heat.IntelBonus(_run.HeatLevel)` with no mission term; src/Run.cs:570-575 IntelBonus(8) = 8×3 + 64/2 = 56. So an h8 campaign banks +56 at m1 and +56 at m2 (≈112 intel, two full requisition slates at the shop costs in Game.cs:401-408) against a force carrying none of the ladder's bodies/stats/damage. DEVLOG §FUL-13 intel table: h8 earned 197.6/run with heat-bonus 112.0 — i.e. the average h8 run's ENTIRE heat income is m1-2's, because the wall ends most h8 runs at m3-4. Nothing in DESIGN.md or the heat selector copy (Hud.cs:1124, 6159 'Pays +N intel per mission') says the carrot arrives two missions before the stick.

It is not a lever to pull now — h6/h8 already sit under their band floors (L4) and cutting early intel makes them harder — but the next base-difficulty round will misread any intel-side effect unless the split is visible.

Record a candidate lever for the base-difficulty round — IntelBonus(level, mission) following the same 0 / half / full ramp — explicitly NOT to be shipped while h6-h8 are under floor.

findings.title: ELITE's 'Bonus perk' reward (and ADV. TRAINING / event training) lands on a RANDOM eligible survivor — the player takes the +2-body fight and does not choose who benefits
findings.evidence: src/Run.cs TryQueueBonusPerk (between GenerateOffers ~985 and PickPerkPair): `var eligible = Squad.FindAll(u => CountAvail(u) >= 2); var u = eligible[Util.RandInt(0, eligible.Count - 1)];` — Run.AddBonusPerk (Elite card, Game.cs:2596), the ADV. summary: The distributable is in unusually good shape for a solo-dev game: CONTOUR C6 gave it a version stamp read off the assembly (Ship.cs:30-45), an enforced 8-file bundled manifest (Ship.cs:73-82), atomic player-data writes, a publish script that re-proves the binary it built (scripts/publish.sh), and a licence position that is decided, committed and shipped (LICENSE, DISTRIBUTION.md:208). What is NOT in shape is the seam between that artifact and a stranger: the primary DEPLOY SQUAD door is the only intro button drawn with a null key hint even though Enter triggers it (Hud.cs:2601-2615 vs Game.cs:8248-8262); the cold main menu's only resting sentence advertises LAST STAND and the difficulty card reads "0 / MAX UNLOCKED: 0" (Hud.cs:2689, 6114-6126); an unhandled exception or a missing libraylib.so exits with nothing a player can attach (Program.cs:1263 has no catch; ROADMAP.md:2564); the Windows build is a console-subsystem exe (Sightline.csproj:4); README's controls and class tables disagree with the derived key set on six rows; and the release story stops at `<Version>1.0.0` — no tag, no changelog, no versioned or checksummed archive, and a first-launch window that never checks it fits the monitor (Display.cs:733-750). Every item below is S or M and has a headless or screenshot gate; none touches gameplay code, so PAIRTEST byte-identity is the regression check for all of them.

findings.title: DEPLOY SQUAD is the only intro door with no key hint, yet Enter already triggers it
findings.evidence: src/Hud.cs:2601-2615 draws the primary button twice as `DrawOverlayButton(OverlayBtn, btn, Pal.Friend, null, btnIn)` (keyHint = null) while every other door passes one: CONTINUE "C" (2608), TRAINING OP "N" (2627-2628), LAST STAND "L" (2633), WAR ROOM "W" (2643), FIELD MANUAL "K", SKIRMISH "S" (2648), DAILY "Y" (2650), AUDIO CHECK "U" (2656), QUIT "Q". Meanwhile src/Game.cs:8248-8262 in HandleOverlayClick: `bool enter = Raylib.IsKeyPressed(KeyboardKey.Enter); if (!click && !enter) return; ... BeginDraft()` — so Enter on the intro opens the DRAFT. The lead photographed the missing chip on the SIGHTLINE_COLD=1 intro.
findings.problem: A first-time player sees nine doors labelled with keys and the one they are supposed to take labelled with none, so the primary verb reads as mouse-only; at the same time an UNLABELLED Enter starts a campaign, so a player who taps Enter to dismiss the screen is dropped into the squad draft. Both halves are the opposite of 'reads clearly' on the first screen in the game.
findings.proposal: Pass "ENTER" as the keyHint in both DrawOverlayButton calls for DEPLOY SQUAD (check the chip geometry in DrawOverlayButton at Hud.cs:6206 handles a 5-character hint at UiScale 1.2 — DEVLOG:9209-9213 already records the [K]/[U] chips colliding at 120%). While there, route a `Hud.IntroNullHintDraws` counter through whichever intro-drawing self-test exists (CHROMETEST/COLD path) so a future button cannot ship hint-less.
findings.acceptance: `SIGHTLINE_INTRO=1 SIGHTLINE_COLD=1 SIGHTLINE_SHOT=90` screenshot shows an [ENTER] chip on DEPLOY SQUAD; with a save present both [C] CONTINUE RUN and [ENTER] DEPLOY SQUAD chips are visible and do not overlap at SIGHTLINE_UISCALE=3; the self-test asserts `IntroNullHintDraws == 0` and PAIRTEST stays byte-identical.

findings.title: No crash log: an unhandled exception (or a missing libraylib.so) exits with nothing a player can attach
findings.evidence: The live loop `while (!Raylib.WindowShouldClose())` at src/Program.cs:1263 sits in Main with no try/catch — the only catch sites in Program.cs are the FUL-2 save-restore at 1345-1350 and CONTRASTTEST at 2306/2314. The first native call `Raylib.SetConfigFlags` at Program.cs:1018 throws DllNotFoundException if libraylib.so is absent, which is exactly the 'I copied only the executable' case README.md:122-124 warns about in prose only. ROADMAP.md:2564-2565 lists 'No crash reporter and no log file ... there is nothing to attach' as open; DISTRIBUTION.md:253-261's player-data table has no log entry.
findings.problem: A player who double-clicks the binary and hits an exception sees the window vanish; on a desktop launch there is no terminal, so the stack trace goes nowhere. The C6 version stamp exists so a bug report can name a build, but the report has no payload — team-facing triage is guesswork, and 'the game does nothing when I open it' (libraylib.so missing) is indistinguishable from any other failure.
findings.proposal: Wrap the live path (from before InitWindow through the loop) in try/catch; on exception write `crash-<Ship.Version>-<utc>.txt` into `SaveGame.ConfigDir` via `SaveGame.WriteAtomic` (needs no raylib) containing Ship.VersionLabel, RID/OS, Environment.Version, the exception + stack, and Phase/mission/turn if a Game exists; keep the last 5; print the path to stderr and rethrow so the exit code stays non-zero. summary: The tree is in good shape where it counts (Release builds 0/0, the sweep is a real gate since C3, PAIRTEST pins CRN identity), but the continuity layer around it has drifted in exactly the way the repo's own history warns about: hand-maintained registries and counts. CLAUDE.md still says Game.cs is 4707 lines when it is 8317 — larger than the 7648 it was split from — its file map omits eight files including Mission.cs, it carries two duplicated paragraphs one of which still publishes the refuted free-key list, and both copies tell a fresh session to grep Program.cs for the dial set when 37 of 226 dials are read only elsewhere. The sweep launches TUTTEST and THREATTEST twice, its COVERAGE GUARD counts hook names that appear in comment lines (so a commented-out test still reads as run) and cannot see the PASS/FAIL PROBE hook, and it pays a `dotnet run` launch 79 times where publish.sh already runs the binary directly. Three invariants CLAUDE.md states in prose (no direct DrawTextEx, no raw GetTime outside Now(), render purity) have no static backstop even though FXSTREAM shows the pattern costs three lines. The mechanical extractions (Game.cs banner blocks, the 10k-line harness, Program.Main's 1386 lines) all have the same cheap verification path the project already trusts: build 0/0, sweep green with an unchanged footer, PAIRTEST byte-identity.

findings.title: The sweep's COVERAGE GUARD counts hook names in comment lines and cannot see the PASS/FAIL PROBE hook, so a commented-out or removed test can still read as run
findings.evidence: scripts/qa-sweep.sh:212-216 computes `_missing` as `comm -23 <(names in src/) <(grep -ohE 'SIGHTLINE_[A-Z0-9_]+(TEST|GATE)' scripts/qa-sweep.sh)` over the WHOLE script including comments; lines 13, 16 and 114 already name AUDIOGATE, FUL11PROBE and EXPOSURETEST inside comments. findings.problem: The guard is the mechanism the repo relies on to make 'every self-test runs' machine-checked instead of hand-counted. summary: The instrument is in far better shape than its own docs admit: chunks now run in ~3 s (every L4 report.txt prints "batch wall-time: 2.6-3.7s" for 20 campaigns), so the 8-slot-set / n=160 convention that makes every rung resolve only 13-14 points is a historical artefact of the old 10-minute shell ceiling, not a cost constraint — a 16-slot-set rung is ~50 s and a full 2^3 factorial at h6 is ~6 min. Two contaminations the docs describe qualitatively are quantifiable from the archived L4 JSONs without running anything: the Events.cs AddHeat leak raised heat in 12-17 of 160 campaigns per rung (7.5-10.6%), putting 3.6-5.6% of missions at heat+1 on every rung below 8 (0% at h8, exactly the directional compression CLAUDE.md warns about), and it is the bot's VALUE-BEST arm on FACTION INFORMANT (+2.0 vs +0.4 vs 0 in Game.cs EventOutcomeValue), not the 30% exploration; the STALEMATE floor is 16/960 (1.7%, not the documented 2.1%) and is concentrated at RECRUIT (7/160 = 4.4% of the rung, 15.6% of its losses; ex-stalemate RECRUIT reads 75.2 vs 71.9) with zero at h6/h8 — so the top-of-ladder collapse is real game, not harness. Three instrument defects block the open balance items: RunRec.Heat is the pinned heat and never the played heat (the leak is invisible at run level though the per-mission byHeat table has carried heat-7 rows in every h6 chunk all along); the STALEMATE cause string conflates the per-mission 50-turn arm and the run-scoped 150-turn arm; and pairedPolicy.slots is empty for any single-policy batch, so a camping-policy batch would leave no per-slot rows for CRN pairing. The measurement-first order is: land the heat pin + per-run rows + stalemate split (all CRN-inert except the pin, which is itself measurable as an exact identity on ~90% of L4's campaigns), re-baseline as L5 at 16 slot sets, run the h6 factorial to resolve the +5.8 interaction, sweep Heat.MidTooth modes 1/2 (never run on the composed tree), re-measure the ladder, then add the camping policy on the final tree.

findings.title: Pin Events.cs AddHeat for measured batches and make the leak a reported number — it is the bot's preferred arm, not exploration
findings.evidence: src/Events.cs:458-462 (`run.HeatLevel = Heat.Clamp(run.HeatLevel + ...)`, no RNG draw) reached from three arms: relic:0 (Events.cs:176), informant:1 (Events.cs:233), reservecall:1 (Events.cs:269). src/Game.cs:7971 prices AddHeat at -4 while Intel is 0.3/pt, so on FACTION INFORMANT 'Turn them in' scores +2.0 against 'Buy the dossier' +0.4 and 'Let them go' 0 — it is the 70% VALUE-BEST arm in Game.AutoEventChoice (Game.cs:7910-7930). Quantified from the archived L4 chunk JSONs: heat-raising arm picks per 160-campaign rung = RECRUIT 16, h0 17, h2 16, h4 13, h6 12, h8 14 (informant:1 = 66 of 88 below h8), and byHeat mission rows at a heat other than the pin = 4.2% / 4.9% / 5.6% / 4.6% / 3.6% / 0.0% for RECRUIT..h8 (e.g. L4-h6-b0.json byHeat carries `{'heat': 7, 'n': 4}`). src/Stats.cs:419-429 stamps RunRec.Heat once at BeginRun (Game.cs:1770) and never updates it, so byHeatRun cannot see any of this. At RECRUIT the leak lands on heat 0 and flips FOUR valves at once: the -1 body/-1 stat RecruitMod (Run.cs Active()), DownedTimerTurnsNow +2 (Game.cs:3310-3311), the m1 checkpoint ckMin (Game.cs:4177), and UpdatePressure's heatBump (Game.cs:6345).
findings.problem: Every rung below 8 is contaminated UPWARD by 7-11% of its campaigns while h8 is clamped, so the instrument compresses exactly the top-of-ladder region L4 says collapsed (h6 10.6 vs floor 12), and RECRUIT — the on-ramp a first-time player meets — is measured with ~10% of its campaigns silently converted into heat 0. Nobody can tell from a chunk JSON how much of a rung was played at the rung.
findings.proposal: Add a static `EventCatalog.HeatPinned` (default false) that makes the AddHeat case return 'Heat pinned (harness)' without mutating HeatLevel; BalanceBatch (Program.cs:1415) sets it true unless `SIGHTLINE_HEATPIN=0`. Because AddHeat draws no RNG, the pinned batch replays L4's exact worlds and differs only on the ~10% of campaigns that leaked — so the pin is CRN-verifiable as an identity on the other 90%. Add `RunRec.HeatEnd` (set in EndRun from `_run.HeatLevel`) and a `heatLeak { campaignsRaised, missionsAbovePin, pinned }` block to BuildSummary so a chunk states its own contamination. Keep EVENTTEST (Events.cs:689-694) untouched — it runs with the pin off.
findings.acceptance: (1) `SIGHTLINE_EVENTTEST` still PASS; PAIRTEST PASS. (2) Re-run L4's 48 chunks from the same `runbin/L4`-equivalent binary with the pin ON (~2.5 min): every campaign whose eventChoicePicks contain no heat-raising arm is bit-identical to L4 (0 discordant pairs on those slots), and `heatLeak.missionsAbovePin` reads 0 on every chunk vs 12-32 with `SIGHTLINE_HEATPIN=0`. (3) Publish the pinned-vs-leaky delta per rung as the first row of the L5 README.

findings.title: n is cheap now: chunks take ~3 s, so 16 slot sets per rung and a factorial at h6 replace the unresolved +5.8 interaction with a measured one
findings.evidence: Every docs/measurements/l4/*.report.txt ends `batch wall-time: 2.6-3.7s (20 matches across 10 campaigns x 2 policy)`; CLAUDE.md's timing table agrees (~5 s per SIGHTLINE_BALANCE=10 under xvfb since W1). docs/measurements/c1/README.md:66 explains the N<=10-per-chunk rule (disjoint slot bases) but nothing limits chunks per rung; L4 used 8 bases (run_ladder.sh) purely because L3 did. docs/measurements/l4/README.md: 'at n=160 with 8 clusters a rung resolves roughly 13-14 points' and the interaction term is 'chunk-paired t(7)=+2.05, p~0.08 ... it needs more slot sets, not more prose'. attribute.sh only ran one-lever-OFF arms; no two-way cell was ever measured.
findings.problem: The ladder of record cannot distinguish a rung 1 point below its floor from one 10 points below, and the most interesting claim in L4 (levers do not compose) is unresolved — both for want of ~10 minutes of compute that the project still budgets as if it were the pre-W1 300-500 s per chunk.
findings.proposal: Standardise a rung at 16 disjoint slot bases (SIGHTLINE_BALANCE_BASE 0,10,...,150 with N=10 -> n=320/rung, ~50 s) via a `docs/measurements/l5/run_ladder.sh` that loops c1/run_chunk.sh; extend c3/cluster.py to 16 bases. Then a 2^3 factorial at h6 over MIDTOOTH{0,3} x AIDECLINE{0,1} x BIOMEMECH{0,1} (KILLTREADMILL measured 0.0 at h6 in L4 and can be dropped): 8 arms x 16 chunks x ~3 s ~ 6.5 min, driven through run_chunk.sh's EXTRA=. Analyse chunk-paired (per slot-set win-rate differences, paired t on 16 clusters) and report main effects + the three two-way terms with cluster SE.
findings.acceptance: A `docs/measurements/l5/factorial.md` table with 8 cells, each `runs=320` asserted (all three layers of the W1 contract via run_chunk.sh), and the MIDTOOTH x AIDECLINE interaction reported as an estimate with a chunk-paired t on 16 clusters. 'Resolved' = either |t| >= 2.3 or a CI that excludes the +5.8 claim; ROADMAP's 'RESOLVE THE INTERACTION TERM, or stop citing it' item ticked either way.

findings.title: The STALEMATE floor is 1.7% not 2.1%, is concentrated at RECRUIT (4.4% of the rung, 15.6% of its losses), and the cause string cannot say which cap fired
findings.evidence: Summed from the L4 chunk JSONs' instrumentHealth: stalemateLosses = RECRUIT 7, h0 3, h2 3, h4 3, h6 0, h8 0 = 16/960. Ex-stalemate ladder: 75.2 / 54.1 / 33.8 / 22.3 / 10.6 / 4.4 — RECRUIT moves 3.3 points, the top rungs move zero. Four of the seven RECRUIT stalemates sit in one chunk (L4-hR-b60: lossCauses {'STALEMATE': 4, 'RUN OVER': 4}) whose Escort row reads 14 missions at 78.6% and 20.6 avg turns; pooled RECRUIT Escort is 13.1 turns vs 7.1-8.3 at h0-h6. The guard at src/Game.Autopilot.cs:1929-1934 fires on `_turnCount > AutoMaxTurns (50, Game.cs:4275) || RunTurns > AutoMaxRunTurns (150, Game.cs:4293)` and logs both as `LoseRun("STALEMATE", ...)`; Stats.RunRec (src/Stats.cs:130-160) carries no RunTurns, no mission number and no objective at loss, so the archive cannot separate the two arms. docs/ROADMAP.md:2653 and DEVLOG:11165 quote '20 of 960' and CLAUDE.md quotes '2.1%'.
findings.problem: The rung a first-time player is steered onto (Game.cs:1895 opens FirstTimeProfile on RECRUIT) is the one the harness misreads most, and the fix cannot be aimed because two different caps share one cause string. The documented figure is also stale.
findings.proposal: Split the cause into `STALEMATE-MISSION` and `STALEMATE-RUN` at the guard, stamp `RunTurns`, `_run.Mission` and `Objective` onto RunRec in Stats.EndRun (Game.LoseRun already passes the title), and add them to `instrumentHealth`. Then reproduce: the b60 chunk covers slots 60-69, so `SIGHTLINE_AUTOPLAY=1 SIGHTLINE_HEAT=-1` with Util.Reseed(50000+slot) for slots 60-69 (or a one-off `SIGHTLINE_BALANCE=10 SIGHTLINE_BALANCE_HEAT=-1 SIGHTLINE_BALANCE_BASE=60`) isolates the stalling campaigns; the Escort turn counts point at the leash/zone livelock family SmartEscort already documents (Game.Autopilot.cs:852, 927, 2028). Fix the bot's finishing line, not the cap.
findings.acceptance: `instrumentHealth` names the arm; RECRUIT stalemateLosses <= 1/160 on the same 8 slot sets; every other rung reproduces L4 with 0 discordant pairs (an autopilot fix must be inert where it did not fire); CLAUDE.md/ROADMAP figure corrected to the measured value with the per-rung concentration stated.

findings.title: Single-policy batches leave no per-slot rows in the archive — the camping policy (and any SLOPPY=1 batch) cannot be CRN-paired offline until BuildSummary exports per-run rows
findings.evidence: src/Stats.cs:599-608 PairList keeps a (slot, heat) only when it has exactly one 'greedy' and one 'sloppy' leg; src/Stats.cs:1765-1784 BuildPaired emits `pairedPolicy.slots` from that list and nothing else per campaign. docs/measurements/c1/ladder.py load() reads ONLY `pairedPolicy.slots[].greedyWin/sloppyWin`. Program.cs:1492-1495: `SIGHTLINE_BALANCE_SLOPPY=1` produces a sloppy-only batch, i.e. an empty slots list and no per-campaign outcome anywhere in the JSON. RunRec already holds Slot, Policy, Heat, Win, MissionsCleared, LossCause (Stats.cs:130-165) — the data exists in memory and is discarded at export.
findings.problem: The ROADMAP's camping policy is 'instrument work that must land BEFORE any wave that claims to have priced turtling', but a third policy cannot be a third leg of the pair (PairList would still pair greedy/sloppy and drop it), so it must run as its own batch — and today such a batch writes no per-slot outcome, so it cannot be paired against the greedy batch that replayed the same worlds.
findings.proposal: Add a `campaigns[]` array to BuildSummary with one row per RunRec: slot, policy, heat, heatEnd, win, missionsCleared, lossCause, runTurns. Teach ladder.py a `--rows` mode that pairs two prefixes by (slot, heat) from that array. Zero gameplay effect (export only).
findings.acceptance: c1/inert_diff.py on a before/after chunk shows no change on any existing key (the harness{} block excluded); `SIGHTLINE_BALANCE=10 SIGHTLINE_BALANCE_SLOPPY=1` yields 10 rows; ladder.py --rows reproduces L4's paired table exactly from a greedy+sloppy chunk.

findings.title: Camping policy for the flywheel: a concrete third policy, and the order swap in SmartCombatStep that makes turtling measurable
findings.evidence: src/Game.Autopilot.cs:1149-1154: SmartCombatStep calls `SmartApproach(u)` (advance pull toward the nearest foe, Game.Autopilot.cs:1678-1683) BEFORE `HoldOverwatch(u)`, and the comment at :1139-1141 records 'the R1 reading proved HoldOverwatch below is unreachable in open combat'. `Slip()` (Game.cs:4233-4238) is hard-gated on SmartSloppy, so sloppy is an error model only. The anti-turtle clock reads `_turnCount` (Game.cs:599-604, grace 4, rung per 2 turns, max 4) and Stats.RecordPressure keeps a per-mission high-water mark (Stats.cs:217-220, exported as `avgPressure` at :1739); ROADMAP:2643-2650 states the measured mean high-water rung is 1.50 and the reinforcement arm now never fires on Eliminate (Game.cs:573-577 ClockMayReinforce). SIGHTLINE_HVTPOLICY (Program.cs:142-145) is the existing precedent for an autopilot-only policy dial.
findings.problem: C3 weakened the clock on the 41% slowest Eliminates and nothing in the instrument can price the result: both policies advance, so the aim arm's bite at rungs 2-4 has never been exercised by a bot that camps. Until it is, no wave can claim the clock works (DESIGN.md §3.A's charter).
findings.proposal: Add Game.SmartCamp (Stats.Policy 'camp', chosen by `SIGHTLINE_BALANCE_POLICY=camp`, same seeding as greedy so it replays greedy's worlds until the first different action). Under camp, on PressureClockObjective() missions while `Pressure < PressureMax`: run HoldOverwatch before any approach, and replace SmartApproach with SmartReposition (Game.Autopilot.cs:1687, no advance pull); once rung == PressureMax or no enemy is Active within reach for 2 turns, fall back to greedy routing so the match still resolves (AutoStallCheck's 50-turn arm stays as the backstop). Run camp as its own batch at 6 rungs x 16 slot sets (~5 min) after finding 4's per-run rows exist.
findings.acceptance: avgPressure on Eliminate/Hack/Decapitate >= 3.0 under camp vs ~1.5 greedy (the policy demonstrably reaches the rungs); camp-vs-greedy CRN-paired win rate per rung with discordant counts; stalemateLosses under camp not above greedy's. findings.title: Heat.MidTooth back-off: modes 1 and 2 have never been run on the composed tree, and only h6/h7 can move — a 4-arm round is ~3 minutes
findings.evidence: src/Run.cs:374-382 `Heat.MidTooth` is a bitfield (1 = +1 dmg to rung 6, 2 = coordination tier 2 to rung 6, shipped 3); Program.cs:115-122 parses SIGHTLINE_MIDTOOTH. docs/measurements/l4/attribute.sh measured only `SIGHTLINE_MIDTOOTH=0` (+6.2 at h6, 10.6 -> 16.9). CLAUDE.md records C1's pooled estimate that coordination tier 2 is +1.09 +-0.63 (indistinguishable from zero, wrong-signed) while the +1 damage is the bite. Run.cs:408-425 Rung6/Rung7/Rung8 show that at heat 8 DmgDelta sums to 1 and AiTier maxes to 2 in every mode, and heats <= 5 never touch rung 6 — so h4 and h8 are bit-identical across modes by construction; only h6 and h7 can differ.
findings.problem: The ROADMAP's top balance item ('the dial to reach for first is Heat.MidTooth') has a partial-back-off candidate (mode 2: hand down coordination, keep the +1 dmg at the apex) that C1's own numbers predict recovers most of the +6.2 while preserving the no-dead-row invariant — and it is unmeasured.
findings.proposal: After findings 1 and 4 land: 4 arms (MIDTOOTH 0/1/2/3) at h6 and h7, 16 slot sets each, via `EXTRA="SIGHTLINE_MIDTOOTH=<m>" bash docs/measurements/c1/run_chunk.sh L5mt<m>-h6-b<B> 6 <B> 10` (BIN=runbin/L5, OUT=docs/measurements/l5), plus one h4 and one h8 chunk per mode as the apex-neutrality assertion. Then the full 6-rung ladder on the chosen mode (96 chunks, ~5 min). One lever, then re-measure, as the L4 README demands.

MIDTOOTHTEST still PASS (no dead row, no silent rung) for the shipped mode. Full ladder re-measured with the heat pin ON and published as L5 with base commit and n.

findings.title: 'Re-tune Mission.OpenerTrim' is mis-specified: the unlosable opener came from the reinforcement arm, and OpenerTrim=0 would push h0 ~15-20 points under band
findings.evidence: src/Mission.cs:609 `OpenerTrim = 1`, applied at :678-679 (m1 -1 body, m2 -1 body). CLAUDE.md §X2: OpenerTrim moved heat 0 from 35.0% to 57.5%; L4's h0 is 53.1 (band 47-63) WITH the trim. docs/DESIGN.md:816-818 and ROADMAP:2618-2640: '22 of the 24 mission-1 losses in 960 baseline campaigns were the reinforcement wave', i.e. the mechanic C3 removed via Game.ClockWavesOnEliminate (Game.cs:568, SIGHTLINE_KILLTREADMILL=1 restores) — not the trim. L4 attribution: KILLTREADMILL=1 moves h6 by exactly 0.0. C3's stratified table: h4's whole gain was opener; RECRUIT..h4 had 0 m1 losses in 640 campaigns.
findings.problem: The ROADMAP item names the wrong dial. Backing OpenerTrim out restores X2's U-shaped curve (m1 75% at h0, the front-loaded anxiety DESIGN §3.D forbids) and drops h0 out of band; restoring the reinforcement arm restores a camping punishment that killed 4-rookie squads for being slow. Neither is 'stakes' — and no m1 target has ever been written down.
findings.proposal: First declare the m1 target as a band (e.g. m1 loss 3-8% at h0, 8-15% at h4, 0-3% at RECRUIT) in DESIGN.md. Then a 2x2 (OPENERTRIM {0,1} x KILLTREADMILL {0,1}) at h0/h2/h4, 16 slot sets, reading `byMission[mission=1]` and `byNodeKind Start` (Stats exports both) — and only then choose, possibly a third option (OpenerTrim=1 on m1 only, 0 on m2) that neither existing dial expresses.
findings.acceptance: m1 win rate inside the declared band at RECRUIT/h0/h2/h4 AND all six rungs still inside their bands on the same L5-shape round; the ROADMAP item rewritten to name the lever actually chosen and its measured m1 effect.

findings.title: The bot's tie-break jitter draws from the shared world RNG, so CRN pairs diverge through draw COUNTS, not through actions
findings.evidence: src/Game.Autopilot.cs:1670 `score += Util.RandRange(0f, 2f); // tie-break jitter` inside ScoreDestTile, called once per candidate tile per MoveToBestTile sweep (Game.Autopilot.cs:1703-1723). Util.Rng is the gameplay stream the batch reseeds per slot (Program.cs RunOne: `Util.Reseed(50000 + slot)`); the sloppy perturbations deliberately use a separate `_sloppyRng` (Game.cs:4229-4238) precisely to avoid correlating slips with the game's dice. W1 severed presentation from this stream for the same reason (CLAUDE.md §W1).
findings.problem: Any instrument or policy change that alters how many tiles get scored (a camping policy, a reposition-vs-approach swap, even a candidate-loop refactor) re-deals every subsequent combat roll in the world, so a 'gameplay-inert' change can show discordant pairs and a paired policy contrast carries world noise it need not carry. It also makes the camping batch of finding 5 diverge from greedy at the first move rather than at the first different decision.
findings.proposal: Route the bot's jitter through a dedicated `_botRng` seeded per slot alongside SeedSloppy (e.g. 2000 + slot), used only by autopilot scoring. This is a deliberate W1-class break (every archived CRN world re-rolls) and must NOT ship alone — fold it into the L5 re-baseline so the break is paid once, and record it in the L5 README the way W1 was recorded.
findings.acceptance: PAIRTEST PASS; an A/A batch is identical; a policy-flip probe (greedy vs camp on one slot) logs the first divergent turn and it coincides with the first differing action, not turn 1. L5 README states the break and that L4 is incomparable to L5.

findings.title: The measurement-first order of operations and the exact L5 protocol (what 'done' means against the band)

findings.problem: Three instrument items and three balance items are open and each ROADMAP entry says 'before the other', but no single place gives the sequence, the commands, the n, or a stopping rule — so the next session risks spending a lever round on a leaky rung again.

(B) Publish `runbin/L5` from that commit; `docs/measurements/l5/run_ladder.sh` = 6 rungs x 16 bases (0..150 step 10) x N=10 = 96 chunks, ~5 min, all `runs=20` asserted; also the same 48 L4 chunks with SIGHTLINE_HEATPIN=0 as the bridge row. (C) h6 factorial (finding 2). (D) MidTooth mode sweep and ladder (finding 6). (E) OpenerTrim 2x2 (finding 7). (F) camping batch on the final tree (finding 5). Every chunk: `mkdir -p .xdg; export XDG_CONFIG_HOME=$PWD/.xdg/<tag>; rm -f <out>.json; EXTRA=... SIGHTLINE_BALANCE=10 SIGHTLINE_BALANCE_HEAT=<h> SIGHTLINE_BALANCE_BASE=<b> SIGHTLINE_BALANCE_JSON=<out>.json xvfb-run -a -s "-screen 0 1280x800x24" runbin/L5/Sightline; test $? -ne 2; assert runs==20`.

findings.title: Analysis tooling is scattered across wave directories and each script reads a different JSON slice — consolidate before L5
findings.evidence: docs/measurements/c1/ladder.py (paired win tables, reads pairedPolicy.slots only), docs/measurements/c3/cluster.py (cluster SE, hard-codes BASES = 8 values and RUNGS), docs/measurements/c4/paired_t.py and aggregate_nodekind.py (chunk-paired t, node-kind cells), docs/measurements/c1/inert_diff.py (inertness). l4/README.md's cluster-SE column was produced by c3/cluster.py pointed at a different directory; none of them reads instrumentHealth or the ex-stalemate rate (`runWinRateExStalemate`, Stats.cs:1357, is written to every chunk and quoted by no script).

summary: The audio layer is now well-instrumented (A1's device-free AUDIOGATE/AUDIODUMP, A2's mastering + voice pool + limiter, A3's AUDIO CHECK screen) but the CUE VOCABULARY underneath it never grew: 23 recipes exist, and in a fight roughly 30 distinct events are funnelled onto five UI cues — `over` fires for 14 different things (overwatch, brace, focus, MARK, SUPPRESS, MOMENTUM, CONTACT!, ARTILLERY INCOMING, enemy overwatch/brace), `reload` for 15 (stabilize, hack, charge set, beacon, patch/revive, four abilities, enemy reload, medic heal), and `turn` for every one of 27 banners. Because those cues are categorised "ui" they ride the UI fader, so a player who turns UI down silences pod wakes and enemy telegraphs. Music is a two-bed crossfade with a four-valued intensity that goes to full combat on every enemy turn even when no hostile is awake (a 0.5 s WaitAnim + banner guarantees a pump per turn), and all eight biomes share one bed. The campaign end fires a legacy jingle and a stinger simultaneously (the loss pair is two saw descents a semitone apart), and the gate's stack list does not contain the explosion stack, a barrel chain, or that double fanfare. Visually the board is strong (V1-V3, W4, W7), but the unit STANCE layer still predates the glyph-chip idiom: OW/BRC/R&G/BLZ/AIM/SUPP/ROUT/WVR are 10-11 px hue-only words, the enemy HUNKER diamond is painted in Pal.Good, and three roles (objective gold, suspicious amber, VIP gold) sit within CIE76 ΔE 9-12 of each other while the selection ring, muzzle flash and OW badge all borrow objective gold. Post-FX residuals in ROADMAP (vignette/CA on the chrome, the inert POSTFX demo hook) are real and have a cheaper fix than the recorded third pass.

findings.title: One 'over' cue carries 14 meanings, 'reload' 15, 'turn' every banner - and enemy telegraphs ride the UI fader
findings.evidence: Recipe intent: src/Audio.cs:281-285 (`over` = "OVERWATCH set: a tense rising two-note"), :203 (`reload` = mag out/in), :296 (`turn` = "the round changes hands"), and the audition caption src/Audio.cs:1388 (`over => "overwatch set, two notes"`). Call sites for `over`: src/Game.cs:3045 (overwatch fires), :3515 and :3552 (MOMENTUM +1 ACTION), :4472 (CONTACT! pod wake), :5327 (MARK), :5642/:5689/:5710/:5747 (overwatch/focus/brace/focus), :6101 (SUPPRESS pin), :6171 (SUPPRESS ability), :7033 (ARTILLERY INCOMING - comment literally says "a charge 'whine' stand-in"), :7133 (enemy BRACED), :7154 (enemy OVERWATCH). `reload`: :3431 STABILIZE, :5781 CHARGE SET, :5792 HACK, :5842 custodian re-arm, :5874 BEACON, :5948 reload, :6129/:6144/:6151/:6158 RUN&GUN/SLIPSTREAM/BLITZ/STEADY, :6201/:6219 PATCH/REVIVE, :7173/:7221 enemy reload, src/Anim.cs:861 enemy medic heal. `turn`: src/Game.cs:2849 inside ShowBanner (27 call sites incl. "VIP DOWN", "AMBUSH!", "POD ROUTED", "CAPTIVE FREED", "ENEMY TURN", "PLAYER TURN"), :6321 reinforcements, :6351 pressure, :7655/:7696 shop proceed. `select`: :4377 CONTACT? sting, :5935 EXTRACTED, ~40 menu confirms. `hunker`: src/Anim.cs:111 SHOVE, :747 SMOKE, src/Game.cs:5255 BARRICADE. Explosions have no voice: src/Anim.cs:529-530 grenade = `crit`+`death`, src/Game.cs:3693 siege and :3738 barrel = `crit`+`death`, src/Anim.cs:767 FLASH = `crit`, :799 INCENDIARY = `crit`. `hit` is the WAR ROOM purchase confirm (src/Game.Meta.cs:88,139,156,169) and `miss` the refusal buzzer; `kill` stinger is the endless WAVE arrival (src/Game.Endless.cs:102). Bus routing: src/Audio.cs:70-74 `IsUiCue = CatOf(id)=="ui"`, src/Audio.Analysis.cs:419-428 puts `over`/`turn`/`reload`/`hunker`/`select` in "ui", so Display.VolUi=0 mutes CONTACT!, AMBUSH!, ARTILLERY INCOMING and every enemy overwatch/brace/reload telegraph. Barrel shot fire (src/Anim.cs:473) is the only PlayWeapon with no pan.
findings.problem: Player-facing: the ear cannot tell a pod waking from a soldier setting overwatch, an ability from a reload, a grenade from a crit, or the enemy's telegraph from the player's own verb - the same rising two-note plays for 'I am ready' and 'they are coming'. The banner cue is so overloaded (VIP DOWN and PLAYER TURN share it) that it carries no information. Turning the UI fader down to quiet menu ticks silently removes combat-critical alerts. Team-facing: the AUDIO CHECK screen's captions describe recipes, not jobs, so the owner auditioning `over` cannot know it is also MARK/SUPPRESS/CONTACT - the instrument built to make audio fileable cannot see this class of bug.
findings.proposal: Add ~7 recipes with one `Reg` line each in BuildRecipes (src/Audio.cs:181): `alert` (contact/ambush - short minor-2nd stab + noise hit, 'impact' bus), `alarm` (reinforcements/pressure/artillery - descending two-note, impact bus), `boom` (explosion - 40 Hz sub thump + 300 Hz wash + 0.4 s debris tail; replaces crit+death at Anim.cs:529, Game.cs:3693/:3738), `ability` (bright engage chirp for R&G/BLITZ/STEADY/SLIPSTREAM/MARK/SUPPRESS), `tick` (objective progress - data blip for HACK/CHARGE SET/BEACON/INTEL), `mend` (STABILIZE/PATCH/REVIVE/medic heal - soft warm two-note), `ui_ok`/`ui_no` (shop confirm/refusal, replacing `hit`/`miss`). Give ShowBanner a `cue` parameter (default `turn`) and pass `alert`/`alarm` from the danger banners; give the ENEMY TURN banner a descending variant (`turn_enemy`). Register each in SfxCueIds, AuditionGroups, CueRole, CatOf (alert/alarm/boom = impact bus, never ui), DefaultPitchVar. Move enemy `over`/`hunker`/`reload` call sites onto the SFX bus by routing them through a `Audio.PlayFoe(id)` that uses VolSfx. Pan the barrel shot. Update assets/sfx/CREDITS.txt drop-in list.
findings.acceptance: (1) `SIGHTLINE_AUDIOGATE=1` prints PASS with 30-31 cues, all inside their category bands, all four+ stacks under -1 dBFS (stacks extended per finding 3). (2) `SIGHTLINE_AUDITIONTEST=1` PASS (every new id listed, captioned, fits at 120%). (3) `grep -c 'Audio.Play("over")' src/Game.cs` drops from 14 to <= 7 (only true overwatch/brace/focus sites) and `Audio.Play("reload")` from 14 to <= 3; `grep -c 'Audio.Play("crit"); Audio.Play("death")'` = 0. (4) A new `SIGHTLINE_CUETEST=1` leg: a table `Audio.CueFor(GameEvent)` is injective over {Contact, Ambush, Reinforce, Explosion, Ability, Objective, Mend, Overwatch, Turn, EnemyTurn} and none of the enemy-telegraph events resolves to a "ui"-bus cue. (5) AUDIO CHECK screenshot (`SIGHTLINE_AUDITION=1 SIGHTLINE_SHOT=90`) shows the new rows; `SIGHTLINE_AUTOPLAY=1` x3 clean.

findings.title: Music pumps to full combat on every enemy turn of a quiet board, and intensity is blind to danger
findings.evidence: src/Game.cs:3869-3878 `MusicIntensity()`: `case Phase.EnemyTurn: return 1f;` unconditionally, while PlayerTurn is gated on `Enemies.Any(e => e.Alive && e.Active)` (0.5 / 0.15) and everything else is 0. src/Game.cs:6407 sets EnemyTurn, :6426-6427 `ShowBanner("ENEMY TURN")` + `Enqueue(new WaitAnim(0.5f))` - so an enemy turn with zero active hostiles still lasts >= 0.5 s at intensity 1. src/Audio.cs:449-456 crossfade `k = dt*2.2`, targets `ambT = 0.5-0.22*I`, `combT = 0.62*I`: after 0.5 s the combat bed has climbed 1-e^-1.1 = 67% of the way to 0.62 (~0.41) and the ambient has dipped 0.50->~0.35, then both slew back over the player turn. With all pods dormant (the normal opening of every mission; pods spawn dormant per docs/ROADMAP.md:41-46) this repeats every turn. No term anywhere reads squad HP, hostiles-with-LoF, last-soldier-standing or heat; the only inputs are Phase and 'any active enemy'. Music is a menu/fight invariant otherwise: intro/barracks/win/lose all read 0 (src/Game.cs:3877).
findings.problem: Player-facing: a rhythmic swell-and-fade of the combat bed on every turn of a board where nothing is awake - the music announces a fight that is not happening, then retracts. Once contact is made the bed cannot tell a 4v1 clean-up from a last soldier at 2 HP, so the layer that should carry 'stakes that bite' is flat exactly when the stakes rise. Team-facing: nothing measures the crossfade; the AUDIO CHECK screen sweeps it by hand only.
findings.proposal: (a) Gate EnemyTurn on the same `Enemies.Any(e => e.Alive && e.Active)` predicate (return 0.15 when nothing is awake). (b) Make the intensity continuous: base 0.5 in contact, +0.25 when any soldier is <= 1/3 HP or downed, +0.25 when the squad is outnumbered by active hostiles, 1.0 on the last soldier standing or enemy turn in contact; clamp 0..1 (`Game.MusicIntensity` is presentation-only and read once per frame at src/Game.cs:3930, so this touches no sim state). (c) Slow the release: asymmetric `k` (dt*2.2 up, dt*0.8 down) so the bed does not drop the moment a turn ends. (d) `SIGHTLINE_MUSICTEST=1`: build a Game headless (the STALLTEST pattern), stage a board with only dormant pods, step Phase PlayerTurn->EnemyTurn->PlayerTurn while sampling `MusicIntensity()`; assert max <= 0.15; activate a pod and assert monotone rise to >= 0.5; down a soldier and assert >= 0.75; assert Audio.MusicLevels time-to-90% within [0.3, 2.0] s in both directions using a scripted dt loop over `UpdateMusic` (device-free: the lerp math runs before the Raylib calls, so guard those on `_music`).
findings.acceptance: `SIGHTLINE_MUSICTEST=1` prints PASS with the four assertions above, and prints FAIL when `MusicIntensity`'s EnemyTurn arm is reverted (prove the test fails pre-fix, per W9 house rule). `bash scripts/qa-sweep.sh --full` green with the new hook in its COVERAGE GUARD. Autoplay x3 clean. A SIGHTLINE_BALANCE=10 paired batch is inert (MusicIntensity is never read by sim code - verify with `inert_diff.sh`).

findings.title: Campaign win/lose fire a legacy jingle and a stinger at the same instant (the loss pair clashes by a semitone); the gate's stack list misses the real worst cases
findings.evidence: src/Game.cs:2609 `Phase = Phase.Win; Audio.Play("win"); Audio.PlayStinger("victory");` and :2738-2741 `Audio.Play("lose"); ... Audio.PlayStinger(... ? "squadwipe" : "lose")`. Recipes: src/Audio.cs:302 `win` = Arp {523,659,784,1046} step 0.11 s, Tri, vol 0.30, and :323-324 `st_victory` = Arp {523,659,784,1046,1318} step 0.11 s, Tri, vol 0.28 - the same four notes at the same step, phase-coincident (a +6 dB chorus with comb interference, not two layers). :304 `lose` = Arp {392,330,262,196} Saw vs :336 `st_lose` = Arp {440,349,277,220} Saw: G4/A4, E4/F4 (semitone), C4/C#4 (semitone), G3/A3 - two saw descents a semitone apart, simultaneously. src/Audio.cs:1379-1402 captions already call `win`/`lose` "legacy". Gate stacks src/Audio.Analysis.cs:245-253 are four rows; not measured: the explosion stack `crit+death` (src/Anim.cs:529-530), a chained-barrel detonation (src/Game.cs:3738 fires `crit`+`death` per barrel, synchronously, plus `death` per body from KillUnit :3210 and a `st_kill` per player-credited body :3790 - a 3-barrel, 3-body chain is >= 12 coincident cues), `win+st_victory`, `lose+st_lose`, `lose+st_squadwipe`. The limiter (src/Audio.cs:803-835) makes this safe but AUDIOGATE's 'stack clipping == 0' claim is being made on a list that omits the loudest stacks in the game.
findings.problem: Player-facing: the two ceremonial moments of a run - the finale and the wipe - are the only places the mix is deliberately doubled, and the loss is accidentally dissonant in a way no recipe designed. Team-facing: the budget's headroom contract is asserted over four stacks while the game's actual worst alignment (a barrel chain) is unmeasured, so the 'nothing leaves over -1 dBFS' story rests on the limiter rather than the budget.
findings.proposal: Delete `Audio.Play("win")` at src/Game.cs:2609 and `Audio.Play("lose")` at :2738 (the stingers own those beats); route the barracks mission-complete at :2658 through `PlayStinger("victory")` or a new lighter `st_clear` so it ducks the bed. Retire `win`/`lose` recipes from SfxCueIds and AuditionGroups (append-only is not a constraint here - cue ids are strings, not persisted ordinals). Add stacks to `Stacks`: ("grenade crit+death"), ("3-barrel chain", 3x(crit+death)+3x death+3x st_kill at 0 s), ("victory: st_victory alone"), ("wipe: st_squadwipe+death x2"). Print the pre-limiter peak per stack so the owner can see which rows the limiter is actually catching.
findings.acceptance: `SIGHTLINE_AUDIOGATE=1` PASS with >= 8 stacks; the new barrel-chain row's peak is printed and either <= -1 dBFS or explicitly listed as limiter-bound (the gate must not claim headroom it does not have). `grep -n 'Audio.Play("win")\|Audio.Play("lose")' src/*.cs` returns nothing. `SIGHTLINE_AUDITIONTEST=1` PASS (new stack names fit AudStackW=300 at 120%). `SIGHTLINE_AUDIODUMP=1` no longer emits win.wav/lose.wav.

findings.title: Unit STANCE states are hue-only 10-11 px words (OW/BRC/R&G/BLZ/AIM/SUPP/ROUT/WVR) and the enemy HUNKER diamond wears the friendly Good colour
findings.evidence: src/Renderer.cs:3984-3990 overwatch = a 6 px disc + `Cfg.Text("OW"/"BRC", ..., 10, ...)`; :3992-3993 `if (u.Hunkered) DrawPoly(..., Pal.Good)` with no team check, while enemies hunker at src/Game.cs:7177, :7182, :7228; :4006-4008 `R&G`/`BLZ` (Pal.Accent) / `AIM` (Pal.Good) at 11 px text only; :4009-4010 `SUPP` 11 px Pal.Foe; :4013-4014 `ROUT` 11 px Pal.Good on an ENEMY; :4020-4023 `WVR` 11 px Pal.Suspect (this one does ship a crack glyph). Three friendly defensive states - hunker diamond, BRC badge, AIM tag - are all Pal.Good with no distinguishing shape beyond a 6 px poly; SUPP (:4010) and PINNED (:4345) are two different mechanics rendered as two red 11 px words. Contrast the newer idiom: src/Renderer.cs:3271-3366 `DrawUnitStatusChips` draws BRN/BLD/STN/DAZ/DRY/DOWN as 13 px pills with a per-state glyph in a late opaque pass. docs/DESIGN.md §3.H: "Rule for any new coded state: ship its glyph in the same pass, and verify it in both palettes". docs/ROADMAP.md:2577 (C5) already records the 12 px floor breach (10 px on AUDIO CHECK, 11 px on seventeen surfaces) as open; this finding is the shape-redundancy half, which is not recorded.
findings.problem: Player-facing: at a squint the actionable difference between 'this enemy is suppressed' and 'this enemy is routed' is one red word vs one green word at 11 px, and a hunkered hostile carries the same green diamond the player's own hunker does - the 'good for me' hue on a state that is bad for me. In the colorblind palette Good becomes teal and Foe orange, and the 11 px words are the only channel. summary: SIGHTLINE's content inventory is wide on paper (22 hostile archetypes, 35 authored arenas, 8 biomes with 3 mechanical, 8 objectives, 4 deployment shapes, 3 factions with mid-boss and finale kits, 17 field events, 16 boons, 5 contracts, 23 perks) and the FUL-9 no-repeat arena deck, hashed objective plan and W4 shapes already deal it well inside the campaign. Where variety runs out first is not the pool sizes but the DEAL: the biome sequence is a fixed 8-cycle with a run offset (only 8 of 56 biome adjacencies ever occur, 1-3 mechanical rooms per run in fixed slots), the climax skeleton is identical every run (mid-boss on m3/m5 by mission number, the map's ELITE node is just +2 bodies), and two of the four modes never see the roster at all: SKIRMISH and DAILY build with n=1, so SelectArchetype hands them SCOUT/GRUNT only, with no faction, no pods of 3 and no kit. Inside the bestiary, 12 of 22 hostiles carry the same SMG and four pairs are stat twins whose only difference is one Ai.Plan weight, while the four most distinctive contest archetypes (BOMBARD/WARBRINGER/PIKEMAN/CUSTODIAN) are 0.8-2.1% of spawns and CUSTODIAN is a dead mechanic on six of eight objectives. The five paint biomes are honestly declared and BIOMETEST-asserted; the cheapest symmetric additions are a VOID rift (a new impassable-but-transparent geometry class) and ARID soft sand (a CostMap-only inverse of ice). Arena exposure numbers in the L4 archive are quantized by 80 CRN seeds and must not be read as generator bias; EXPOSURETEST is the right instrument, and the report has no per-run content-exposure block at all.
